text:
maria: Heads-up: I'm seeing a weird import break for the Python SDK when contributors use Poetry's editable install. Quick repro: run `poetry install` in the sample app, then `python -c 'import redwood_sdk; import redwood_sdk.asyncio'` -> raises ModuleNotFoundError for redwood_sdk.asyncio. The built wheel in CI looks fine.

sam: Is this happening on PEP 660 editable backend specifically? Poetry delegates to pip's editable wheel builder now. There were past issues where packages declared in pyproject don't match files on disk, so subpackages get dropped. Can you paste pyproject.toml?

maria: Here's the minimal pyproject:```toml
[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood-sdk"
version = "0.0.0"
packages = [ { include = "redwood_sdk" } ]
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.8"
```
We have normal layout with `redwood_sdk/__init__.py`, `redwood_sdk/asyncio/__init__.py`, `redwood_sdk/typing/__init__.py`. When I `pip wheel .` locally the wheel contains subpackages, but `poetry install` editable ends up installing only the top-level package file and subpackages are missing in the environment. This varies across machines.

josh: Two quick checks: 1) confirm this isn't an implicit namespace package case (PEP 420) which can confuse editable backends; 2) verify Poetry/core version — older versions had regressions for editable installs.

maria: Not using namespace packages. All subdirs have __init__.py.

sam: Run these in both envs and paste results: `python -c "import redwood_sdk, pkgutil; print(list(pkgutil.walk_packages(redwood_sdk.__path__)))"` and `pip show -f redwood-sdk`. That should show what ended up on disk.

maria: In poetry env the pkgutil output lists only `redwood_sdk` root and `pip show -f` shows just `redwood_sdk/__init__.py` and a tiny set of files. In a pip editable env (`pip install -e .`) it shows everything.

dev-bot: CI job #6912 shows "ERROR: Invalid wheel tag for platform" on macos-arm build. Log: https://ci.example/6912 — probably different issue but flagging.

josh: Sounds like Poetry editable is truncating package discovery. Concrete fixes: make packaging explicit. Try in pyproject:```toml
[tool.poetry.packages]
include = "redwood_sdk"
```
Or use `include = ["redwood_sdk/**", "py.typed"]` under `tool.poetry` so files like py.typed get packaged. Also run `poetry self update` to get latest editable backend.

katie: Also make sure `py.typed` is present at package root and included via `include` stanza. Missing py.typed causes typing consumers to fail and some packagers to omit files.

maria: We had py.typed but maybe it's not being included. Our tests didn't catch editable-vs-wheel differences.

sam: Workarounds until we fix pyproject: `pip install -e .` is more reliable for editable installs. Alternatively, contributors can `poetry build && pip install dist/*.whl` to match CI behavior. But we should fix the source metadata.

josh: I'll add a CI smoke test that runs `poetry install` in a clean venv and does `python -c 'import redwood_sdk.asyncio'` as part of devex matrix. That will catch regressions.

katie: I'll draft a small dev doc about recommended local workflows (we prefer `pip install -e .` for faster feedback, but include steps for Poetry editable if you must). Also propose a tiny packaging checklist for PRs that touch package layout.

maria: I'll open a quick PR updating pyproject to explicitly list packages and include py.typed and add an include glob for subpackages. Linking PR after creation.

sam: FYI: If you use `packages = [ { include = "redwood_sdk" } ]` vs `[tool.poetry.packages]` table, behavior can vary across Poetry versions. Explicit table is safer.

maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/1310 (adds explicit [tool.poetry.packages] include + `py.typed` in include list and a note in contributing docs). Please review.

josh: Reviewing now. Thanks for the clear repro and test plan. Also let's track the macOS ARM wheel tag error separately (CI link).

katie: I'll add the CI smoke test in a follow-up PR and update the dev onboarding doc to call out editable pitfalls. :thumbsup: 

maria: Thanks all — will post back if any contributor still sees missing subpackages after PR merge. If so I'll prepare a minimal repro repo.

josh: Glad this surfaced. Small packaging metadata changes avoid a lot of confusing local dev pain.
